title: The relative profinite test functor over an affine component space
statement:
Let $T$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $S=\pi_0(T)$ be its space of connected components with the quotient topology [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite], and use the small pro-etale site $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ be the category of profinite spaces over $S$ with finite jointly surjective covering families. For a continuous map $S'\to S$ of profinite spaces, choose a cofiltered presentation $S'=\varprojlim_i S_i$ over $S$ in which each $S_i\to S$ is pulled back from a map of finite sets along a finite clopen quotient of $S$. Each $T\times_S S_i$ is the finite disjoint union of the corresponding clopen subschemes of $T$, with their restricted structure sheaves. The affine-transition inverse limit
$$T\times_S S':=\varprojlim_i(T\times_S S_i)$$
exists as an affine weakly etale $T$-scheme, is canonically independent of the presentation, and is functorial in $S'\to S$. This functor preserves finite limits and finite coproducts and sends covering families to pro-etale coverings. It defines a geometric morphism $\pi_T:\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{proet}})\to\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\mathrm{proet}})$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. If $q_S:\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\mathrm{proet}})\to\operatorname{Sh}(*_{\mathrm{proet}})$ is the slice projection from the profinite site over $S$, then $p_T\cong q_S\pi_T$, where $p_T$ is the condensed-point morphism [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback].

proof.text: A compatible continuous map W → E gives the continuous lift w ↦ (W.hom(w),g(w)) into the pullback space. Apply the stalk-isomorphism lifting theorem to obtain a unique scheme morphism. The pullback homeomorphism identifies uniqueness with equality of the E coordinate.

proof.text: For S ×_C A, lift each actual restricted clopen open subscheme into the test object. The finite A coordinate identifies the image with its open fibre. The lift is an embedding because its composite with the structure map is the open inclusion, and is a stalkwise isomorphism by cancellation. These disjoint open immersions cover the test scheme, so their cofan is a coproduct in schemes and in schemes over T.

proof.text: For any small relative limit cone, apply the right-adjoint inclusion of profinite spaces into topological spaces, and its slice functor. A cone of T-schemes gives a cone of continuous maps through the profinite projections. Its unique topological limit map lifts uniquely to a scheme morphism by the mapping property. Checking the projections proves the scheme limit, with no need to restrict or glue affine tests.

proof.text: For a finite coproduct in the profinite slice, the images of the coproduct injections are open embeddings of the pullback spaces and stalkwise-isomorphic scheme maps. They are disjoint and cover, so their cofan is a scheme coproduct. Reflection through the forgetful functors gives preservation in the weakly etale slice. Reindex a finite covering family by Fin n and apply the component-site covering clause.

proof.text: Let G be the relative functor following S times a profinite space, regarded over T, and H the absolute profinite test functor. Continuity implies preservation of finite coproducts by pulling back representable sheaves and using the extensive topology. Finite limits identify the image of the singleton with the terminal T-scheme. Consequently both finite restrictions are canonically finite copowers of T. The relative-limit result and the absolute test-object theorem show preservation of the canonical finite-quotient limits. Extend the finite comparison naturally, then cancel the fully faithful forgetful functor to compare the site functors.

proof.text: Mathlib Over.forgetAdjStar induces an adjunction on sheaves between overPullback and restriction along Over.star. Since restriction preserves finite limits, it defines the slice geometric morphism q with the exact required inverse image. The component evaluation datum supplies π and its direct image as restriction.

proof.text: Restriction along the preceding natural site-functor comparison, together with composition of continuous sheaf pushforwards, identifies (π.comp q).direct with the direct image adjoint to profinitePointSetSchemeInverseImage T. Apply the conjugate isomorphism correspondence for the two adjunctions to obtain exactly the inverse-image isomorphism in the statement.
